courseName: MGT 527: The Strategic Management of Nonprofit Organizations

definitions.individualExercise: Many individual exercises are listed throughout the syllabus, attached to specific lectures. They are prompts to think through before class — you do not submit all of them. Four of them must be submitted as videos over the course of the semester, and which four is your choice. If you prepare a video for a given class, you should be prepared to discuss it in class.
definitions.individualExerciseVideos: Four required video submissions, chosen by you from the exercises marked in the syllabus. Each video is a maximum of three minutes and answers that lecture's individual exercise question. Record with Zoom or any simple platform. Videos must be submitted on Canvas by 9:00 p.m. the evening prior to that class. Submit as a video file or Zoom cloud recording link. Speaking directly to the camera is sufficient; you may briefly share a screen or hold up a figure, and may upload a supplementary exhibit to Canvas. AI tools may be used in preparation, but the video itself must show you, an actual human, speaking to the camera. Strongest videos draw on specifics from the case. Worth 45% of the grade.
definitions.projects: All students must, individually or in a group of up to 5, create a presentation video of no more than 15 minutes. Topics must be cleared with the professor. Choose from three general project areas: (1) evaluate a strategic challenge or opportunity facing a nonprofit or group of nonprofits; (2) student nonprofit entrepreneurs pitch and develop a new nonprofit idea with a group; (3) choose a nonprofit area and analyze an actual or potential innovation, including how project evaluation should take place and impediments to adoption and evaluation. Preliminary topic areas are due September 17 so the professor and TA can match-make teams. Worth 35%.
definitions.project2Presentation: Students who choose Project 2 (the nonprofit entrepreneurship track) must additionally present their work live in class on Tuesday, December 15, 2026. Nonprofit entrepreneurs will be asked to present their pitches to the class.
definitions.classParticipation: Students are expected to come to class prepared and to actively engage, bringing their own experiences to the course material. Worth 20%.
definitions.aiPolicy: You may use AI outside of class as much as is helpful. The classroom is device free — all devices put away. For video assignments, you should look like a human speaking conversationally to the camera; explaining something in your own words is the point, and reading aloud makes for a painful video.

gradingPolicy: Class Participation: 20%; Projects: 35%; Individual Exercise Videos: 45%. The syllabus is marked 'Draft and Subject to Change' and notes that visitor schedules in particular may change.
